text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on continuous-batching streaming path (us-west-2). Auto-threshold triggered at 14:03 UTC. Affected service: /v1/stream/generate. Current p99 = 6.2s (SLO 2.0s). Paging oncall group now.

Mina Lee: ack, I'm on it. grabbing logs + links. Anyone seeing customer pages?

SupportBot: Two customer pages: AcmeGames (timeouts > 60s for streaming sessions) and MedForms (partial degradations). Both on us-west-2.

Mina Lee: triage plan: 1) confirm whether cont-batch queue is building due to mixed sequence lengths 2) check scheduler fairness + per-worker batch sizes 3) if needed, route streaming traffic to fallback low-latency variant and throttle batcher.

Raj Patel: oncall takeover in 10m if still active. Mina, can you paste the top hot traces?

Mina Lee: quick dump from the batcher metrics:
```
batcher.queue_length: 142 (normal < 20)
batch.size.p95: 48
batch.size.p99: 128
streaming.active_sessions: 980
avg.seq_len: 420 tokens (wide tail)
worker.kv_cache_evictions: spike -> yes
```
Looks like mixed long sequences + big batches. p99 batch size hitting 128 which aligns with the tail.

Diego Morales: attention: we pushed model-build with larger max_batch_size yesterday to improve throughput for embeddings. Might have bumped cont-batch config inadvertently. Checking recent deploys.

Lucy Chen: I see routing skew: ~70% streaming went to pool cont-batch-prod-usw2-a which has older kernel. The other pool has preemptive-shed enabled. So fairness broken.

Mina Lee: mitigation candidates (short):
- set max_batch_size=16 on cont-batch-prod pools (immediate)
- enable preemptive_shed for streaming requests (shed longest sequences)
- isolate streaming to dedicated nodes with smaller batch cap
- fallback: route streaming to low-latency variant `gptx-small-ll`

Raj Patel: agree. Prioritize config patch + routing fallback. I'll run the patch and watch p95/p99. Mina, can you draft the customer impact blurb for Support?

Mina Lee: yes. Draft: "We're investigating increased latency on streaming endpoints in us-west-2 caused by batching interaction with mixed long sequences. Engineers are applying a live mitigation to reduce batch caps and enable preemptive shedding. We expect latency improvement within 5-10 minutes. We'll post updates every 15 minutes and notify customers if their sessions are impacted beyond 30 minutes." Thoughts?

SupportBot: Posted to the two affected customer contacts. Support will escalate if we need to issue credits.

Raj Patel: executing commands now:
```
# lower batch size on both pools
redwoodctl config set cont-batch-prod-usw2-a.max_batch_size=16 --env=prod --apply
redwoodctl config set cont-batch-prod-usw2-b.max_batch_size=16 --env=prod --apply
# enable preemptive shedding on streaming route
redwoodctl route update /v1/stream/generate --preemptive_shed=true --env=prod
```

Mina Lee: running quick healthcheck on streaming route after config change:
`curl -s -X POST https://us-west-2.api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/healthz` -> `{"ok": true, "latency_p99": 5.9}` (still high, give it 30s for rolling apply).

Diego Morales: I rolled back the embed throughput patch on cont-batch-prod-usw2-a (it had a config change to max_batch_size=256). That should stop new large batches from forming.

Lucy Chen: scheduler logs show a packing loop that favored newer nodes because of stale topology info. Pushing a quick scheduler refresh to the fleet.

Raj Patel: routing fallback to `gptx-small-ll` in progress: `redwoodctl route split /v1/stream/generate --traffic 25%:75% --variants=primary,gptx-small-ll`

IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: action completed: config patches applied and routing split executed at 14:07 UTC.

Mina Lee: monitoring p95/p99 now. initial: p95=1.9s, p99=5.8s. After config patch and routing split (14:08): p95=1.7s, p99=3.1s. Progressing but p99 still above SLO.

Raj Patel: enable temporary stream timeout extension clients => no, don't change protocol. Instead increase routing to fallback to 50% while we drain backlog.

Raj Patel: `redwoodctl route split /v1/stream/generate --traffic 50%:50% --variants=primary,gptx-small-ll` -> applied.

Mina Lee: p99 dropped to 2.1s after 50/50 (14:12). p95 steady at ~1.5s. Looks like backlog clearing and long sequences being shed.

Diego Morales: dug into trace samples: long seqs are mostly from one customer job that rewrites logs into huge prompts. Flagging that customer with Support to throttle or batch client-side.

Lucy Chen: note: KV cache evictions spiked earlier; we should add a follow-up to investigate cache sizing and eviction policy for mixed seq workloads. Filing ticket after incident.

Mina Lee: handing off to Raj for monitoring and post-incident writeup. I'm going to step out to brief PM. Key follow-ups:
- root cause: oversized max_batch_size + scheduler fairness + mixed long-seq workload causing large batch packing and tail latency
- short fixes applied: lowered max_batch_size, enabled preemptive_shed, routing split to low-latency variant, aborted embedding throughput roll on one pool
- customer impact: AcmeGames and MedForms experienced timeouts and degraded streaming sessions; Support notified and initial blurb posted
- follow-ups: cache eviction analysis, scheduler topology bug, improve batcher telemetry by per-seqlen bucketing, add automated fallback when p99>3s

Raj Patel: taking post-incident. Will run a 1hr watch window and then create the incident report. Assigning follow-ups: Diego -> cache & config audit; Lucy -> scheduler refresh/root cause; Mina -> customer comms and postmortem blurb.

SupportBot: Customer contacts acknowledged. AcmeGames requests a postmortem. Marking as P1 for customer comms.

IncidentBot: Paging cleared for oncall group at 14:18 UTC.

Raj Patel: updating thread summary in ops channel and will create JIRA: RED-INC-2026-0314. If anyone sees regressions ping me directly.

Mina Lee: thanks team. Resolved for now, keeping watch. :thumbsup:

Lucy Chen: adding note — consider per-route batch caps for streaming vs batch endpoints to avoid cross-impact.

Diego Morales: adding a filter to ingestion pipelines to limit absurd prompt lengths as a medium-term guardrail.

Raj Patel: handoff complete. I'll post the postmortem skeleton within 2 hours and add metrics snapshots. Leaving thread open for any late regressions.
